issues.claim: implications_for_consultancy[0]: a firm is 'already budgeting $300-$900/month for coverage (Alert's own blog) and is used to annualising that to $4,500-$10,800'
issues.problem: $300/month annualised is $3,600, not $4,500. The low end of the annual figure does not follow from the sourced monthly range (Alert's blog: $300-$900/month). Only the ceiling ($900 x 12 = $10,800) is arithmetically correct.
issues.fix: Restate as '$3,600-$10,800 a year' (or '$300-$900/month, i.e. $3,600-$10,800 annualised'). Keep the inference label.

issues.claim: implications_for_consultancy[6]: 'a $250-$400/month after-hours AI-plus-backup offer lands below Alert's $240 message-taking tier while including qualification'
issues.problem: Internally contradictory: a $250-$400/month offer is above, not below, Alert's $240 Basic tier (verified at alertcommunications.com/plans: Basic 'Starting at $240/month', 100 minutes, message taking). The pricing recommendation and the comparison it rests on cannot both stand.
issues.fix: Either reprice the offer (e.g. '$150-$230/month to sit under Alert's $240 message-taking tier') or drop the 'below Alert's $240 tier' justification and instead anchor it under Ruby $250 / Abby $164-$329 and above Smith.ai AI Pro $150. State which number the claim is measured against.

issues.claim: offerings[Alert Communications].setup_fee: 'Not stated on plans page'
issues.problem: Incomplete. The plans page footnote states 'Additional usage, overages, setup fees, and add-ons may apply', so the vendor does signal that setup fees exist, just not an amount. As written a reader may conclude setup is free.
issues.fix: Change to 'Amount not published; page footnote says additional usage, overages, setup fees and add-ons may apply. Vendor blog itemises a typical ~$500 setup (CRM integration $200, custom scripts $150, agent training $150).'

issues.claim: offerings[Answering Legal] setup_fee / contract_terms cite source_url https://www.answeringlegal.com/help-center/billing/how-does-answering-legal-s-pricing-work
issues.problem: That help-center page does not contain the $399-$599 extensive-setup reserve, the $350 Dec 5-Jan 7 trial setup fee, the $21.50 carrier recovery fund, the 1.5%/month late fee or the first-six-months review. All of those are in https://www.answeringlegal.com/terms-of-service (last modified April 10, 2026), which I opened and confirmed - the figures are right, the citation is not.
issues.fix: Add https://www.answeringlegal.com/terms-of-service as the source for the fee/contract terms and keep the help-center URL only for the feature-inclusion and month-to-month claims it actually supports.

issues.claim: price_ranges.mid_market: A Message Center grouped among 'general-market/per-call options'
issues.problem: Classification only, not a price error: A Message Center markets itself as a law-firm answering service (amessagecenter.com/legal-answering-service, 'Serving law firms since 1962'). Its $145 price is legitimate as the mid-market floor, but the label misdescribes the vendor.
issues.fix: Move A Message Center into the legal-only group, which would make the legal-only band $145-$675 and require the $240-$675 sub-band sentence to be restated (Alert Basic $240 and LEX Entry $375 are the floor for vendors with no cheaper tier; A Message Center Standard $145 is lower).

issues.claim: offerings[Lawmatics] presents the grid as Essential and Premium at a '3 user minimum'
issues.problem: The vendor pricing page shows a user-minimum row reading 3 / 3 / 5, i.e. a third, higher plan (10,000 contacts, 5-user minimum) exists above Premium. The brief's two-tier summary is incomplete and the blanket '3 user minimum' is not true of the whole line. No price is misquoted (all Lawmatics plan prices are quote-only).
issues.fix: Add the third tier (5-user minimum) or state 'Essential and Premium carry a 3 user minimum; the plan above Premium has a 5 user minimum'.

issues.claim: buyer_reported_costs entries sourced to Reddit (r/Lawyertalk $225/$440/~$10 per call; r/LawFirm $429/250 min; $299 for 50 calls) and the BBB Smith.ai complaint
issues.problem: Could not be independently reopened: Reddit returned 'could not extract readable content', BBB returned HTTP 403, exactly as the brief discloses. The figures remain unverified search-summary anecdotes.
issues.fix: Keep, but the brief's own caveats should be repeated wherever these figures are used downstream; do not let them into any range or recommendation as if they were vendor prices.
